Sublime crew

By: Tarryn Crossman | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
They’re not your typical dance moms.
They’re not sitting on the sidelines cheering — they’re on the floor, throwing down.

Sublime is a hip-hop dance crew made up entirely of Women over 35. Most are in their 40s, some in their 50s — and they can seriously move. Between raising kids, full-time jobs, Financial stresses and everything in between, they’ve made space to chase a dream.

And not just chase it — smash it.
They’re the current Hip Hop Unite World Champions.

Proof that rhythm, grit, and a love for dance don’t come with an age limit.

Further information:
Some of the warrior in sneakers are
Terri, from Grassy Park, has three boys and works a minimum wage job. But four nights a week, without fail, she shows up to train. When the team qualified for Worlds in Spain, they rallied to raise the money so she could be there.

Simone is the heartbeat of the crew — fundraiser, motivator, spokesperson. She talks beautifully about how dance has become a lifeline for older women — a way to carve out space for themselves, to find joy and purpose beyond the daily grind.

They’re all carrying something — bills, kids, health worries, the weight of life. But when they walk into that studio, they leave it all at the door. For those few hours, it’s just the music, the movement, and each other.

Script:


(Terri) I express myself more, like you can see what I'm feeling by me moving my body.
When it comes to my dance, that’s where I’m in control and nobody else.
So, I own it.

(Terri) My son started dancing at the age of 5.
(Terri) That was when he received his western province
(Erin) Oh wow, And which one is he
(Terri) This is Clayton on the far right
(Erin) Wow, that’s the windmill
(Terri) That’s the signature
(Terri) It was really good watching him grow, getting his South African colours.
They placed like, ninth in the world.

(Corinne) Terri was always focusing on Clayton, and he was flourishing so much.
But she had this love for dance. That's where I think Clayton gets it.

(Erin voice over) Corinne de Beer has coached Clayton Le Roux for nearly 10 years and watched his mother Terri passionately support from the sidelines. So, one day, she asked her to join a class, and dance for herself.

(Terri) she was like, why don't you just give it a try? And I was like, no, man.
Like, my life's over, you know, I've got a son now, we need to. And she was like, no, it's not.

(Corinne) Okay you have two minutes to warm up your ankles, two minutes to warm up your wrist. And let’s get going
(Terri) I Gave it a try. And I didn't stop.


(Erin voice over) And sublime was CREATED.
A 6-woman street dance crew of mostly moms over 40.

(Erin voice over) As a crew, SUBLIME had one goal…. to win the Hip Hop Unite World Championships. The most prestigious dance competition in the world!

(Corinne) This is one of the cream of the crops competition. It's known to bring the, the elite. if you score well or come top 10 in the world, then you know that you're good.

(Erin voice over) And to beat the best of the best, these women had to sacrifice everything to be in the studio. Dance came first

(Terri) Once we commit, we go full tilt
(Chantal McClure) The most important thing is, like I just say to myself every day. is just don’t miss a class. Because it is easy to fall back on excuses. The minute you miss one, it’s easy to miss another one. Just don’t give yourself the option. I am always late, but I’m there. I always make sure I get there.
(Erin)And in terms of your family’s and stuff. What is like the backup team at home?

(Sarah Rennison) At school they always give those pamphlets, like what’s your favorite food and those kinds of questions. And one of them was what does your mom do as a living? and he was like hip hop. That’s interesting. That’s very sweet. So, for the record that isn’t what you do for a living? No, that’s not my day job

(Chantal McClure) They know what the plan is, and they must either fit in or fall out.
(Erin) Is that your way or Coach’s way ?
(Terri) My husband is actually… He does the food at home, he does the washing.
To be honest I don’t think know if I could have actually pulled this without him

(Simon Hepburn) Terri’s husband, Mike, wanted to have a t-shirt printed that siad no dance, just finance.
Because essentially, they are paying for us to travel.
Because when we go overseas and travel as a team they stay at home
So slowly, but surely the husbands become dance husbands

(Chantal McClure) Dance husbands

(Erin voice over) After months of dancing day and night, SUBLIME earned their South African colours and, for the first time in 2020, qualified for the Hip Hop Unite World Championships.

(Corinne) They went, and they came third. And third's not good enough.
We must come first. So, yeah, we came home, and we had quite a short period, like Six months or something that. And we have to do the choreography, we have to train, we have to drill. You've got break dancing, you've got whacking, you've got locking. You've got a whole bunch of different styles in that two minute. And they have to qualify with a certain score in order to go over again.

(Erin voice over) They trained harder and longer. Pushing through fatigue and injury, with one goal in mind… the win the next championship title.

(Erin voice over) Even Terri’s son Clayton joined in, helping the crew refine their breakdance moves and raise the bar.

(Terri) He would train me, would say if there's anything you're struggling with, we can go over it at home, we can gear you up
He's like, you've got this.
You can do this.

(Erin voice over) In 2024, Sublime qualified again and went to Portugel to compete against Elite dancer from over 50 countries.

(Erin voice over) And this time they took home the hip hop unit world championship title

(Terri) There's no better feeling knowing that the sacrifice, the tears, the blood, the sweat, the arguments, the, oh, my word, like. And there's no better feeling like, we've done this.


(Corinne) And it's a dream that they had, I think, to win the world championship. And I think that in itself changes you as a person. The confidence boost, the training process that goes through it that you go through to get onto the world stage.
It’s not just a physical thing, it's an emotional and a mental thing as well. And I think they carry that through as well through their hardships outside of the dance studio.

(Erin voice over) A few weeks ago While SUBLIME were in training for the next shot at the world championship title, Terri’s son Clayton was in a serious motorbike accident

(Terri) the doctor said, I cannot save this child again. after losing him four times

(Terri) all we asked for, was for the second chance for Clayton to live knowing that it might not happen.

(Erin voice over) The team rallied around her. They showed up, at the hospital, at her home and in the studio.

(Terri) He's recovered well, but it's going to be a long and slow process
the trauma doctor said to me last night,
We don't want you to stay positive all the time because we know it's not. We can't have you crack. So think about, what if he can never make a cup of tea again? What if he doesn't even remember was a dancer or even a biker
And so that battle is the battle I'm at.

(Terri) Dance has taught me
how to pull through when you feel like you can't pull through.
especially during this time where I couldn't to run.
Despite how you feel, despite what you going through, you need to go out there, you need to do what you need to do. I can't give up.

(Corinne) we are now starting to work on our next title, so we're going to get back into it now. we're gonna try go back for another third title now. Yeah.
(Erin) Lucky number three.


(Terri) It’s never too late to start. Financially, it shouldn’t stop you, physically it shouldn’t stop you, your age shouldn’t stop you.
(Corinne) You have no limits
if you have a dream, make it happen.
